Open • FLYBYME (Tim) opened about 2 minutes ago • 0 comments
Labels: package


  Six VPS and a laptop, and nothing shows them or decides what they run. The  
  next                                                                        
  milestone needs both, and most of the mechanism already exists in the wrong 
  repository.                                                                 
                                                                              
  ## The Supervisor is in mesh and belongs in mesh-serve                      
                                                                              
  Decided: "move Supervisor out of mesh, that was a mistake, and it goes in   
  mesh-serve because it's part of the serve."                                 
                                                                              
  It is self-contained —  src/supervisor/Supervisor.ts  (424 lines),          
   SupervisorService.ts  (113),  cli/commands/SuperviseCommand.ts , plus tests
  and                                                                         
  fixtures.  mesh/src/index.ts:65-66  re-exports it. Nothing in mesh-serve or 
  paas imports it today, so the move breaks no consumer.                      
                                                                              
  It is also exactly the switch mechanism the fleet needs, already built:     
   supervisor.service_start ,  service_stop ,  service_restart ,              
  service_status ,                                                            
  over a manifest of named entries with  dependsOn ,  mountKey , and per-entry
  database isolation. Assignment is not a new idea — it is "tell node N to    
  start                                                                       
  these manifest entries and stop those."                                     
                                                                              
  ## What the fleet layer adds                                                
                                                                              
   node.hello  /  node.assign  /  node.status , over the Registry's existing  
  presence rather than a second heartbeat.  cdn/schema/edge.ts  already argues
  this and the argument still holds:                                          
                                                                              
  │ Not liveness: no lastSeen, no healthy, no status, no heartbeat... The mesh
  │ already tracks connected nodes via RegistryModule. A second heartbeat     
  │ beside                                                                    
  │ it produces two sources of truth that disagree during partitions.         
                                                                              
  So the row holds desired state — the assignment. Observed state is          
  Registry presence. Same declared/desired/observed shape as everything else. 
                                                                              
  ## Decisions already taken                                                  
                                                                              
  • A node's id is its hostname. Not the per-process  nodeID  the mesh mints  
  ( publish-a7f3k ), which changes every restart. A rebooted VPS is the same  
  row.                                                                        
  • A switch, not a code shipment. Every node carries the same set of         
  services; genesis decides which run. No artifact pipeline for the server    
  side.                                                                       
  • Topology: one VPS binds a public port. Every other node binds 127.0.0.1   
  and dials out to it. This needs a custom runner —  bin/node.mjs  takes flags
  today and assumes it is the only node.                                      
  • Operator, not admin, and they are not the same thing. An organization's   
  admin is not a platform operator.  api/methods/gate.ts:98  has              
   ADMIN_ROLE = 'admin'  and levels  public | user | admin  — there is no     
  operator level.  api/methods/delivery.ts:19-24  already has the concept and 
  its meaning ("a platform operator, who sees across organizations"), so the  
  gate is the half that is missing.                                           
  • Node authentication: a shared key. Today bootstrap is a bare              
   ws://127.0.0.1:4001  with no credential — anything that reaches the port   
  becomes a peer and can call tools. That is acceptable on loopback and not   
  acceptable for a public port.                                               
                                                                              
  Fast detection of an unclean node loss is FLYBYME/surfdns#41, in mesh, in   
  parallel. It is not a blocker for this.                                     


View this issue on GitHub: https://github.com/FLYBYME/surfdns/issues/42
